races.name: Burke's Clonbur 3-Y-O Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Another Day Done
runners_data.note: Flat form entirely on Good ground at shorter trips; this 2m2f hurdle test is a significant step up in distance and the horse's history (four wins on the Flat) does not transfer naturally — hold-up style by nature but redistributed into midfield because the field is stacked with rear-runners, making a clean late run on hurdles debut difficult.|

runners_data.name: Armillary
runners_data.note: Unraced, no form to assess and going preference unknown; lightly raced tag applies in full, and Harry Sexton's 7lb claim could offset some inexperience, but the complete absence of a form line makes this a major unknown in a 16-runner field.|

runners_data.name: Bell Ex Too
runners_data.note: Nine starts without a win or place on similar going; R P Cody's runner has shown nothing to inspire confidence at this trip, and though its natural instinct is to race from the rear, the crowded midfield in this shape will force it forward of its comfort zone — bleak profile on the numbers.|

runners_data.name: Camp Verde
runners_data.note: John Joseph Hanlon has had one winner from 16 runners over 14 days and Camp Verde has faded on all three starts, the most recent a distant eighth in a Flat maiden over 18f; back-end of the field by temperament but the race map will push it mid-pack, compounding its well-documented finishing weakness.|

runners_data.name: Captain Con
runners_data.note: Noel Meade's runner — blinkered here — has finished no better than sixth from six Flat starts on Good ground and was last seen only six days ago; the blinkers suggest connections are searching for a trigger, but the form line over shorter trips is uniformly disappointing and genuine hold-up tendencies will be thwarted by the congested field.|

runners_data.name: Montevetro
runners_data.note: Denis Hogan runner who showed two placed efforts on Standard and one on Good, with the slight form uptick on faster ground worth noting; a natural hold-up type who will need to find room in a packed finish, but the placed form gives it a marginal edge over many rivals here.|

runners_data.name: Point Star
runners_data.note: One run over 18f on Good — fourth — gives a slender thread of form; Mark Fahey's runner has an unknown style profile and the lightly-raced flag applies, though a single outing at this sort of trip is at least relevant to today's conditions.|

runners_data.name: Step By Step
runners_data.note: Aidan Howard debut hurdler, completely unexposed; the headgear (hood) suggests some management on first start and the unknown going preference is a genuine handicap for assessment, though Howard's 1/2 trainer strike rate over 14 days hints at a live runner if ability has transferred.|

runners_data.name: Wills History
runners_data.note: Brian McMahon debutant with no form to go on and an unknown going preference — the going report shows Good to Yielding throughout the card, so the surface at least should be predictable; without any form string to anchor a view, this horse sits firmly in the lightly-raced bracket alongside the other first-timers.|

runners_data.name: Divine Believer
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead's runner — notable for the trainer's 4/26 14-day strike rate suggesting the yard is in form — has finished between fifth and eighth in all five starts on Good or Soft ground; the profile suits a finisher but the redistribution problem in this race means getting a clean run through the compressed field will be the primary obstacle.|

runners_data.name: Misty Cove
runners_data.note: The race's sole confirmed front-runner wearing a tongue-strap for Gavin Cromwell, who has had no winner from 38 recent runners; Misty Cove's best form came when winning over 10f on Soft and showed ability staying 17f, and an uncontested lead here on Good to Yielding over 2m2f is a compelling tactical advantage — the style-fit caveat applies only if challenged early, which looks unlikely.|

runners_data.name: Neon Eyes
runners_data.note: Cromwell's second string, also headgeared (hood), with a second on Good ground from seven starts; showed a flash of form at 10f on Good and may find 2m2f testing, but the nudge of a placed effort at least differentiates it from the blanket of zero-win, zero-place rivals in this field.|

runners_data.name: We're Out Of Aces
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's unknown debutant — the yard is firing at 4/33 over 14 days and Elliott regularly debuts lightly raced types with latent class in these novice hurdles; the complete absence of any form string is a risk, but the trainer angle makes this one of the more interesting blanks in the race.|

runners_data.name: Sonny Corleone
runners_data.note: Five starts without a win, best effort a fourth on Good ground over 10f; Gordon Elliott-trained, unraced for 37 days and showing a natural hold-up profile — the lack of any headgear change and modest form line suggests this is a horse still finding its feet rather than one ready to step forward.|

runners_data.name: Chairmanforlife
runners_data.note: Mrs John Harrington's runner unseated on its most recent start over 17f and has been placed just once from four hurdle runs; the prominent style is a genuine asset in this race shape and the Harrington yard at 2/36 over 14 days is not red-hot, but positional supremacy in a front-run race elevates its chance above its raw form.|

runners_data.name: Matada
runners_data.note: Cromwell's third entry, absent for 111 days — the longest layoff in the field — and has finished 11th–14th in all three starts including on going similar to today; fades in the finish by profile and the long absence adds another layer of doubt, making it difficult to make a case with any conviction.|

races.paceDynamic: Misty Cove is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 16-runner maiden hurdle and will stride into the lead unchallenged, setting a sustainable gallop on Good to Yielding ground over 2m2f that is unlikely to be truly searching. Chairmanforlife is the one horse capable of tracking closely in a genuine prominent role, and the pair will shape the early fractions between them with minimal external pressure. The large field contains a heavy concentration of hold-up types — Another Day Done, Bell Ex Too, Camp Verde, Captain Con and others — who will be forced to race closer to the pace than is natural for them, compressing the midfield and reducing the true gap between prominent and hold-up runners. This race shape strongly favours horses that can travel in a handy position and produce a clean jump at the last, rewarding prominent-to-midfield types who secure a good early berth; true closers are disadvantaged because the horses nominally mapped at the rear are not genuine hold-up specialists and will clog the middle ground, making late runs harder to thread through. The field holds more prominent and hold-up types than can all secure their natural position — Misty Cove and Chairmanforlife are best-placed to actually dictate from the front, while horses like Captain Con and Camp Verde, genuine hold-up types by record, will likely find themselves racing against their instincts in a congested midfield pack.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Misty Cove Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Misty Cove dictates an uncontested, measured gallop and jumps soundly throughout, strangling the race for rivals.
scenarios.body: Jumping cleanly at every hurdle on Good to Yielding ground, Misty Cove's front-running role turns this into a test of jumping accuracy and stamina rather than tactical speed, making it very difficult for hold-up horses to close late through a packed field. Horses that travel prominently and jump well behind the leader are best-placed to pick up the pieces if Misty Cove tires, but none have the profile to reel in a confident front-runner setting its own fractions.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Set Honest Test
scenarios.trigger: If Chairmanforlife or a lightly-raced unknown pressures Misty Cove sufficiently to inject honest fractions from the outset.
scenarios.body: A competitive early gallop begins to sort the field on the climb to the finish, and horses who have shown stamina and a clean jumping technique move through to challenge as the pace-setters feel the pressure. Lightly raced horses with unknown profiles — Step By Step, We're Out Of Aces, Armillary — represent the wildcard danger if they have the class to exploit a genuinely run race.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Lightly Raced Types Emerge
scenarios.trigger: If an unraced or debut hurdle runner steps forward with a superior class profile to upend the established form lines.
scenarios.body: Gordon Elliott's We're Out Of Aces or Aidan Howard's Step By Step, unknown quantities making their jumping debut, could outclass rivals if their flat ability translates immediately to hurdles on this trip and surface. In a moderate maiden where no runner has shown a winning hurdle run this season, a talented newcomer with unexposed potential has genuine scope to dictate the market at the finish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop proves genuinely strong enough to bring hold-up horses into play at the finish, opening a gap on the rail.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires Misty Cove to collapse late and the congested midfield to part sufficiently for a true closer, but given that most hold-up types here are redistributed runners racing against their nature rather than genuine stalkers, the probability of a clean late run materialising is markedly reduced. Divine Believer or Sonny Corleone would be the nominal beneficiaries if the pace truly collapses and the field spreads, but both carry modest form and the scenario is unlikely to unfold cleanly.

watchPoints.text: Misty Cove's jumping under pressure — if the horse makes a significant error at any hurdle while leading, it could halt a race-controlling performance and open the door for Chairmanforlife immediately.

The congested midfield created by redistributed hold-up types (Captain Con, Camp Verde, Bell Ex Too, Another Day Done) risks a significant incident or interference on the turn for home — in a 16-runner field this is a genuine safety concern.

We're Out Of Aces and Step By Step are Gordon Elliott and Aidan Howard debutants respectively — watch for market moves on both in the final 30 minutes before the off, as unraced types from these yards can be well-prepared on debut.

Chairmanforlife's jumping must be monitored closely — a pulled-up run last time (P in recent form) suggests a jumping or jumping-confidence issue that could surface again in a race where it needs to travel prominently throughout.|

Neon Eyes ran only six days ago — watch for signs of fatigue in the second half of the race if it secures an early position, as a quick turnaround on Good to Yielding ground over 2m2f may find it out late.|

races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Mares Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Goodgollymissholly
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a win and two places from five outings on similar Good ground; Gordon Elliott yard in solid form (T14: 4/33) and James Smith claims 5lb — the combination of class and tactical position just off the leader is her strongest suit over this 2m2f trip.

runners_data.name: Maximillian Lady
runners_data.note: Returns after 88 days off for Paul Hennessy with a consistent record of 1W3P from five runs on Good and Soft; Richard Condon (5) claims and she has placed at 16f on soft so the step up in trip and ease in ground should not inconvenience her.

runners_data.name: Brave Lady
runners_data.note: Has been remarkably consistent placing four times from six runs including on Soft ground, but has yet to convert from a prominent position — Peter Fahey sends her here 45 days after last run and the plateau in form is the concern.

runners_data.name: Carleys Lilly
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up mare by profile who is mapped to midfield because the field's density of rear-runners means she cannot get her natural position; John Patrick Ryan's runner has finished in the frame at 18f on Good ground but her chance is tempered by racing outside her comfort zone tactically.

runners_data.name: Certosa
runners_data.note: Has a placed effort at 16f on Good ground and finished second on her most recent outing; Tom Kelly (7) takes the ride and she is one of the more credible hold-up threats if the pace creates late opportunities, though finishing second in a small field is different to running down a leader in an 18-runner contest.

runners_data.name: Hashtag Doyen
runners_data.note: Lightly raced with only two hurdle starts both on Good ground, posting a fourth and sixth; Mark Fahey handler, Thomas O'Connor (7) aboard, and the unknown style profile (U) means she is genuinely unpredictable — a danger only if dramatically better than her form suggests.

runners_data.name: Lunar Majesty
runners_data.note: Has finished outside the frame in all six hurdle starts, most recently sixth at 22f on Good; the longer trip may suit her stamina profile but the consistency of moderate finishes makes it hard to see her breaking through here, even with Ross Berry (7) claiming.

runners_data.name: Mia In Milan
runners_data.note: Tagged as a hold-up runner who fades in the finish — the worst possible combination for this pace shape where the tempo is unlikely to be strong enough to set up a late charge; 94 days off the track for D E Fitzgerald adds further uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Santa Paula
runners_data.note: Has placed twice from five runs, including a third on Good ground over 18f; P J O'Hanlon rides and she has been placed at trips similar to today, but her last two runs produced an 11th and 7th and the form curve points the wrong way.

runners_data.name: Tara Boe
runners_data.note: Flagged as fading in the finish, which undermines a prominent style in a race where the leader controls the tempo; the 8-year-old hasn't finished better than fourth in recent outings and Kevin Sexton takes over from the saddle — the hold-up headgear (hg:h) suggests connections are looking for a different tactical approach.

runners_data.name: The Dotski
runners_data.note: Henry de Bromhead's unexposed 5-year-old returns after 195 days off the track with an unknown style profile; both runs came on Heavier ground at 16f so today's trip and Good to Yielding surface introduce unread variables — the stable form (T14: 4/26) is the main reason to keep her onside.

runners_data.name: Kilbarry Alexy
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner in the race, returning after 251 days off for C O'Keeffe with Danny Power (7) up; limited hurdles form (9th and 3rd from two starts) but the uncontested lead on Good to Yielding ground is a significant tactical gift in an 18-runner field.

runners_data.name: Mastertown Miss
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare who placed (2nd) on Soft ground over 16f most recently; Peter Smithers (5) claims and the David Harry Kelly yard has had two wins from 12 in the last 14 days — she has some claims but is stepping up in trip and needs others to do her pacemaking work.

runners_data.name: Ronnie's Rascal
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer for Willie Mullins with 0W2P from four runs including a second over 22f on Good — the trip here suits and the stable is firing (T14: 3/17); Sean Cleary-Farrell (7) claims and the tongue tie is noted from recent runs.

runners_data.name: Rosarian
runners_data.note: Placed at 19f on Good ground most recently (2nd) for Josh Halley, a yard with one win from six in the past 14 days; Richard Deegan rides and this prominent mare has claims on the form, though her seventh on heavy ground over 17f shows some going sensitivity.

runners_data.name: Lexenna
runners_data.note: Three runs all producing mid-field finishes (6-7-6) on Good and Soft ground for Darren Collins; no jockey listed, unknown style, and no placed form — needs a significant step forward to feature.

runners_data.name: Katie Can't Count
runners_data.note: Lightly raced for Willie Mullins with only two hurdle starts (4th and a fall); the strong stable (T14: 3/17) is a flag but the fall in the most recent run and limited evidence of ability means this is largely a speculative entry — unknown style makes her hard to place tactically.

runners_data.name: Sea Limit
runners_data.note: Tagged as fading in the finish and lightly raced with two consecutive ninths on Good ground; no jockey declared, returns 20 days after last run for Eugene M O'Sullivan — the fade flag combined with poor recent form makes it very difficult to construct a winning scenario.

races.paceDynamic: Kilbarry Alexy is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 18-runner mares maiden hurdle over 2m2f on Good to Yielding ground at Ballinrobe, and with no genuine rival to press her early she should dictate a measured, unhurried gallop from the front. The prominent runners — Goodgollymissholly, Maximillian Lady, Brave Lady, Ronnie's Rascal, and Rosarian — will jostle for position just behind her, creating a competitive but not frenetic early tempo across the first circuit. With a large field of 18 and several hold-up types struggling to find natural positions at the rear, the race is likely to become strung out on the final bend, rewarding those who travel smoothly just off the pace rather than those buried deep. The field holds more prominent and hold-up types than the map can accommodate cleanly — Carleys Lilly, a true hold-up runner, has been redistributed to midfield and is unlikely to get the clean passage from the rear that her style demands. This pace shape — a single uncontested leader setting a sustainable tempo — most strongly favours prominent racers with the stamina to grind home in the closing stages on this easy ground.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Kilbarry Alexy Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Kilbarry Alexy leads unchallenged and the prominent chasers lack the class to reel her in off a steady pace.
scenarios.body: Kilbarry Alexy sets a comfortable gallop that saps the finishing kick of hold-up types who need a stronger pace to aim at, while rivals who chase too hard from prominent positions tire after the last; the Good to Yielding ground rewards a horse who conserves energy through the early stages and gallops on relentlessly.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Reels Her In
scenarios.trigger: If one of the prominent runners travels powerfully enough to close down Kilbarry Alexy approaching the last and sustain a challenge on the flat.
scenarios.body: With a steady pace set up front, a prominent horse like Goodgollymissholly or Maximillian Lady with a strong jumper's action can close smoothly without burning out and hit the line hardest; Ronnie's Rascal's consistent form and Rosarian's recent placed effort also make them threats in this shape if they travel with cover just off the leader.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Finishes Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens mid-race and creates enough of a gap for a true hold-up horse to pick up strongly in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: Certosa or Santa Paula, both of whom have placed form at this level, would need the prominent runners to burn each other out setting up a true run-in test; the redistribution of Carleys Lilly to midfield means she is racing out of her natural role and the scenario depends on a pace shape that the lone front-runner is unlikely to create.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Unexposed Type Improves
scenarios.trigger: If a lightly raced unknown quantity like The Dotski or Hashtag Doyen produces a career-best from an unknown style profile.
scenarios.body: The Dotski is 195 days off the track for Henry de Bromhead and has shown some ability over a shorter trip, while Hashtag Doyen has limited hurdles form to read; both carry significant uncertainty and would need a rough race that disrupts the more experienced prominent types.

watchPoints.text: Kilbarry Alexy gets 251 days off the track and a completely uncontested lead — watch whether Danny Power (7) uses that freedom to dictate a true gallop or allows a dawdle that sets up a sprint finish, as that choice shapes the entire race.

With 18 runners and multiple prominent types including Goodgollymissholly, Maximillian Lady, Ronnie's Rascal, and Rosarian all wanting prominent positions, watch for crowding and interference on the first bend as they all attempt to settle just behind the leader.

Carleys Lilly is a genuine hold-up mare forced into midfield by the field's composition — watch her race with particular attention to whether she finds clear daylight turning for home, as a blocked passage would end any chance she has.

The Dotski is 195 days off the track for Henry de Bromhead (stable 4/26 in 14 days) and has an unread style profile — watch how she is ridden in the early stages as any market move before the off would indicate the yard expects significant improvement.

Tara Boe and Mia In Milan are both flagged as fading in the finish despite holding prominent and hold-up styles respectively — watch whether either capitulates visibly after the last, which would confirm the pace shape ultimately told against horses who needed more of a test.

races.name: Michael Cawe Suspended Ceilings Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Ehteyat
runners_data.note: Prominent racer (OR 121) with form showing place consistency at distances around 2m-2m2f; steps up to 2m6f which is a query — sim-going record of 9/15 and no wins on similar ground suggests conditions are borderline, though Tom Kelly's 7lb claim helps the weight.|

runners_data.name: Needs Must
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott runner off a 178-day absence, which is a major flag; one win and one place from six starts on similar going suggests the ability is there but this comeback run makes him a watch rather than a banker.|

runners_data.name: Arcland
runners_data.note: 10-year-old trained by Gavin Cromwell with a strong recent record including a course win at 2m4f; suited by this trip, excellent sim-going stats (15 runs, 3W 8P), though the blinkered headgear and 15 days since last run suggest he is primed and dangerous from a prominent position.|

runners_data.name: Jupiter Du Gite
runners_data.note: Tracked the front in his last two starts (placed both times over 2m6f+ on good ground), so this trip and conditions suit; hood and front-run tendency mean he should sit prominently, but his trainer's 0/3 recent strike rate tempers enthusiasm.|

runners_data.name: In The Minus
runners_data.note: Young 4-year-old hold-up type with good form at 2m-2m5f on good ground; two wins from 13 runs on similar going, and the step to 2m6f looks within range — a genuine player if the pace scenario creates late openings.|

runners_data.name: Crossing The Bar
runners_data.note: 523 days off the track is the dominant concern, making this effectively a comeback run regardless of his 1W 2m6f/Soft win in recent form history; tube headgear fitted, and Cian Collins's modest 14-day record of 1/10 offers limited confidence.|

runners_data.name: Luck Between Us
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse whose recent form is excellent — won 10 days ago over 2m4f on good ground and placed over today's 2m6f trip; Donncha Duggan's stable is not operating at high volume but Niall Moore (5) claim is useful weight relief.|

runners_data.name: Take The Free
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed front-runner in this race, so gets a clear, uncontested lead; won last time out over 2m4f on good ground and has place form on soft, suggesting conditions and trip are fine — the key question is whether his rivals allow him to coast or test him mid-race.|

runners_data.name: Better Times
runners_data.note: 104-day layoff is a concern for a hold-up horse that needs to build into a race; one win on soft and limited recent evidence from similar going (1W 1P from 11) makes him an each-way speculation at best.|

runners_data.name: Strange Currency
runners_data.note: Consistent low-finisher in recent form (never better than 5th in last 7 starts) whose OR has drifted to 104; genuinely a hold-up horse who will be racing toward the rear, but the redistribution note reflects that the field's back-end is crowded — his chance depends on a strong pace scenario that looks unlikely to materialise.|

runners_data.name: Mr Dibbs
runners_data.note: Recent winner at 2m6f on good ground (Cromwell, same trainer as Arcland) and has distance/trip credentials; however, his natural running style is held-up, meaning he may struggle to produce his best if the moderate pace set by Take The Free doesn't stretch the field enough for a closer to arrive.|

runners_data.name: Mickey Cohen
runners_data.note: Noel Meade's 5-year-old showed progressive form with a win and two places in last five starts; a genuine hold-up horse by nature who tends to need a real gallop to get competitive — he is best served by Scenario C but will likely be further forward than ideal in this low-pressure race.|

runners_data.name: Free Flow
runners_data.note: 7-day turnaround from his last run is an immediate flag; form figures of 090-64 over shorter trips (16-19f) make the step to 2m6f a stretch, and as a hold-up type mapped forward here, the race shape offers him little.|

runners_data.name: Pilgrims Walk
runners_data.note: Shown tendency to fade in the finish — an important flag over 2m6f on yielding ground; placed last twice at the trip (3rd and 2nd), but the fading profile and redistribution into a race shape that won't produce a slow, strung-out gallop limits his chance, with the Paul Rothwell 14-day record of 1/26 adding further caution.|

races.paceDynamic: Take The Free is the single confirmed front-runner in this 14-runner field and, with no meaningful rival to contest the lead, is expected to dictate at a sustainable gallop over the 2m6f trip on Good to Yielding ground at Ballinrobe. Ehteyat, Arcland, and Jupiter Du Gite are the natural prominent types who will attempt to sit just behind, creating a compact early order rather than a charging pace. The tempo should be controlled and even — a genuine test of stamina rather than speed, which historically on this trip and ground favours horses that travel smoothly in behind before producing a sustained run from the second-last. Several runners — Strange Currency, Mr Dibbs, Mickey Cohen, Free Flow, and Pilgrims Walk — are true hold-up types who have been mapped forward because there are more hold-up horses in this field than the rear of the race can accommodate; of these, Mr Dibbs and Mickey Cohen are most likely to actually secure a position toward the rear of the midfield, with Strange Currency the most credible true closer. The race shape strongly favours prominent racers with strong staying profiles who can track the moderate leader and strike from two out.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prompt Leader Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Take The Free dictates an uncontested, measured gallop and the prominent pack never applies serious pressure.
scenarios.body: Take The Free sets a comfortable tempo, the race stays strung out, and prominent horses tracking it — Arcland, Jupiter Du Gite, Ehteyat — are in perfect position to pounce from the second-last hurdle. This shape rewards horses that travel economically close to the pace and have the stamina to grind out the final half-mile on yielding ground.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Land Late
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent horses burn more energy than expected in the early and middle stages, leaving the race open for genuine hold-up types.
scenarios.body: The pace quickens enough through the final circuit to string the field out, and horses held up with gas in reserve find the gaps opening from the last. Luck Between Us and In The Minus, both effective on this ground and trip, are best placed among the genuine hold-up types to capitalise.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Strong Pace Test Stamina
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent pack pushes up on Take The Free mid-race, collectively lifting the tempo into a true stamina examination.
scenarios.body: A genuinely run race over 2m6f on yielding ground becomes a battle of reserves from the third-last, and horses with proven stamina and strong finishing figures come to the fore. Mickey Cohen's consistent place-form and Luck Between Us's recent win at the trip make them logical beneficiaries of this shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Outstays All
scenarios.trigger: If Take The Free is allowed to steal enough of a break that the pursuing pack cannot reel it in over the final climb.
scenarios.body: With no rival capable of matching Take The Free stride-for-stride early, the leader simply extends and the closers find the deficit too great. This scenario is low probability given the class of prominent rivals breathing down its neck but cannot be entirely dismissed.

watchPoints.text: Take The Free — if the leader is completely unchallenged through the first circuit, watch whether the prominent horses (Arcland, Jupiter Du Gite) allow the gap to grow; a five-length break at the top of the home straight could be too much to claw back.

Arcland — at 10 years old, watch whether he travels with his usual fluency in the first half-mile; if he is under pressure to maintain a prominent position before halfway, his chance fades significantly.

Needs Must — Gordon Elliott's runner is 178 days off the track; watch whether Kevin Healy settles him smoothly from the rear, as any early exuberance after such a lengthy absence could compromise his stamina for the long 2m6f trip.

Luck Between Us — coming off a recent win and down in distance to what has been his optimal 2m6f; watch whether Niall Moore uses the 5lb claim aggressively to sit closer to the pace than his hold-up profile suggests, which could make him a live player in either prominent or closing scenario.

Crossing The Bar — 523 days off is a significant absence; watch in the paddock and early running for any signs of ring-rustiness, as a horse returning from that length of break rarely produces peak form first time back.

races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Mares Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Cobra Queen
runners_data.note: A hold-up mare operating off OR 118 for De Bromhead with a conditional aboard; outstanding record in similar going (15 from 15 on Good) and 4 wins over this course/distance profile, though the patient style depends on a proper gallop developing.

runners_data.name: Theflyingbee
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner here, she'll set the pace unchallenged but races off OR 116 with a STYLE_FIT flag (0.93) suggesting she is being placed in a role that may not suit her best form; last won over shorter trips and her jumping needs to be slick to maintain the advantage over 2m6f.

runners_data.name: She'll Be Kept
runners_data.note: Won back-to-back in January including over 2m4f on Soft, giving her the best recent winning form in the race; amateur rider Mr E M Nugent carries a 7lb claim which is a key financial advantage, and she handles cut in the ground well.

runners_data.name: Camlin Park
runners_data.note: A natural prominent racer who should slot in just behind the leader and get a positive ride from Calum Hogan (5lb claim); her course form is solid (sim-going 7 from 7) and 16 days between runs suggests she is fresh.

runners_data.name: Sound Judgement
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott runner with a win over C&D conditions in her recent past; prominent style suits this shape well, and Kevin Sexton takes over, though she was beaten last time on comparable ground and needs to bounce back.

runners_data.name: Nothing Hectic
runners_data.note: A hold-up mare with two wins on similar going in her last five; Ricky Doyle partners her and she's 32 days fresh — she needs the pace to lift late on 2m6f to get competitive, and that is the key variable.

runners_data.name: Bossy Bird
runners_data.note: Carries a finishing fade flag and a STYLE_FIT discount (0.91); her natural style is that of a genuine hold-up horse who has been pushed up to midfield on the map purely by the volume of closers in this field — she has no wins in 7 similar-going runs and her form figures of 8-4258 do not inspire confidence.

runners_data.name: Walkingmayotomilan
runners_data.note: A 5-year-old for Ross O'Sullivan, she won at Ballinrobe in April on Good ground, which is an obvious positive; however her true running style is hold-up, she carries a fade warning and a STYLE_FIT flag, and her placement in midfield on the map reflects the crowded rear rather than her genuine tactical position.

runners_data.name: You Make Me Smile
runners_data.note: Consistent placer (1W8P in similar going) who has strong placed form at shorter trips; naturally a hold-up horse displaced forward on the map, the 36-day absence and 7lb claim from Sean Cleary-Farrell are minor plusses, but she is unlikely to win without a true fast-pace scenario.

runners_data.name: Run For The Border
runners_data.note: Ran third at 2m6f in similar conditions last time and has course form over this sort of distance; a genuine hold-up type shown in midfield purely because of the field's compositional imbalance, and 11 days between runs is very tight — freshness could be a concern.

runners_data.name: St Anthonys Corner
runners_data.note: 345 days off the track is the dominant issue here — no run since last summer, poor form figures throughout her career (best effort a single 4th in 14 runs), and she carries a finishing fade flag; Norman Lee has a 0/4 record over 14 days and this looks a tough comeback assignment.

races.paceDynamic: Theflyingbee is the one confirmed front-runner in this 11-runner mares' handicap hurdle over 2m6f on Good to Yielding ground at Ballinrobe, and with no serious challenger for the lead she is set to control the pace from the front without being pressured into unsustainable splits. Camlin Park and Sound Judgement will seek prominent positions just off her, creating a steady, controlled gallop rather than a true test of stamina — the kind of tempo that can flatter front-runners while leaving hold-up horses with little to aim at late. The field actually contains a significant cluster of genuine hold-up and come-from-behind types — Bossy Bird, Walkingmayotomilan, You Make Me Smile, Run For The Border, and St Anthonys Corner are all true hold-up horses who have been displaced to midfield on the map simply because they cannot all settle at the rear in a race with this shape; the prominent positions will realistically be claimed by Theflyingbee, Camlin Park, and Sound Judgement. With an uncontested front-runner dictating a sustainable pace on fair ground over a thorough trip, this race shape strongly favours prominent racers and horses who can travel close to the pace rather than deep closers who need a genuine gallop to make up ground late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Theflyingbee Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Theflyingbee gets a clean break and dictates an uncontested, honest but manageable tempo throughout.
scenarios.body: She sets every fraction from the front without being headed, and the gallop on Good to Yielding ground over 2m6f is enough to reward those who have tracked her without fully testing the late closers' finishing kicks. Prominent horses who travel smoothly in her slipstream — particularly Camlin Park and Sound Judgement — are ideally placed to pounce, while Cobra Queen and Nothing Hectic are the hold-up profiles best equipped to deliver if they've conserved enough energy.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Strike Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves genuinely searching enough that the true closers get a proper gallop into which to deliver their challenge.
scenarios.body: Cobra Queen and Nothing Hectic, both proven on similar going and over comparable distances, would be best positioned to sweep past a tiring lead pack if they can find a clear run in a moderately competitive finish. She'll Be Kept, with back-to-back wins including one on soft ground, has the stamina profile to stay on powerfully if the pace lifts at the business end.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Front Runner Fades
scenarios.trigger: If Theflyingbee goes too hard too early or the Good to Yielding ground takes a greater toll than expected, triggering a chaotic late finish.
scenarios.body: A collapse in the lead would open the door for those travelling smoothly in behind — She'll Be Kept, a dual recent winner who handles this sort of ground well, and Sound Judgement, who has shown tactical versatility, could be the chief beneficiaries of a scrambled run-in. Walkingmayotomilan, a genuine hold-up type redistributed to midfield, would need everything to fall right but cannot be entirely dismissed on her winning form.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Messy Race, Outsider Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the field bunches, there is interference at hurdles, or the redistributed hold-up types fail to find their natural rhythm and the race falls apart tactically.
scenarios.body: In a muddled contest with no clear beneficiary from the pace shape, Run For The Border — who ran third at this trip and has solid course-form in similar conditions — could emerge late at a price, and You Make Me Smile's consistent placed record gives her an each-way profile in chaos. St Anthonys Corner's long absence and poor recent form make a meaningful contribution here very unlikely.

watchPoints.text: Theflyingbee — if she jumps cleanly and establishes an uncontested lead at her own pace in the first mile, she could be very hard to catch and front-runners operating without pressure are a significant danger on this course.

She'll Be Kept — her back-to-back winning form is the freshest in the field and the 7lb amateur claim for Mr Nugent makes her effective weight competitive; a smooth early position could make her a serious threat.

Run For The Border — only 11 days since her last run is an unusually tight turnaround, and backers should monitor whether she runs freely enough to settle in hold-up position or shows signs of staleness.

Cobra Queen — watch the early market move; De Bromhead hold-up mares with strong similar-going records at this track often attract informed support and her 4W9P record in comparable conditions is hard to ignore.
St Anthonys Corner — 345 days absent with poor career form; if she shows any early reluctance or is sluggish at hurdles, she is likely to be a spent force well before the final circuit.

races.name: P&D Lydon Mares Beginners Steeplechase

runners_data.name: Ad Caelum
runners_data.note: Dropped in OR to 104 giving this 7yo a weight edge, and trainer Ryan has two wins from 14 recent runs; a genuine hold-up horse by inclination who will find himself pushed into midfield by the race shape rather than his preferred rear berth, tempering his finishing threat.|

runners_data.name: Affinity Rock
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the field, this OR 122 6yo has been placed in six of seven runs on similar going and should slot straight into an uncontested lead; Carl Millar (5) has the simple task of keeping her rolling without burning too much fuel over the marathon trip.|

runners_data.name: Carried With Love
runners_data.note: Lightly raced 5yo returning from 222 days off and trained by Jonathan Sweeney, who has had no runners in the past 14 days; she races hold-up in character but will be pressed forward into midfield by the race dynamic, which asks her to operate differently to how she's been placed to best effect in her placed efforts.|

runners_data.name: Cherry Red
runners_data.note: An 8yo who recorded a win at 18f on Good ground but has a notable tendency to weaken in the finish and has been well beaten in most recent starts; 61 days off and a trip of 2m7f on softer ground than preferred looks a combination that asks serious questions.|

runners_data.name: Cooke's Lass
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott runner with a good historical record at 22-25f on Good ground and two wins and a second from five similar-going runs, but she has been off 364 days and her jumping under match pressure must be regarded as an unknown; hg:p (hood) may help focus her.|

runners_data.name: Giorgia Rose
runners_data.note: Emmet Mullins 6yo who wears a hood and tongue-strap and has been placed three times at 22-24f on Good to Yielding — clearly at home in these conditions — and Ricky Doyle gets on well with prominent types; zero wins from five similar-going starts is a minor concern but her track record over this trip is consistent.|

runners_data.name: Joya Del Mar
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up mare who has won twice at 22f on Good or Good To Yielding and shows the best proven form in the going band with 14 runs on similar surfaces; Alix Balfe (7) is a 7lb claimer which adds interest, but the horse's natural closing style is better suited here than several others mapping to the rear.|

runners_data.name: Straight Home
runners_data.note: Willie Mullins-trained 9yo with an outstanding record — four wins from 12 on similar going, including wins over 22f and 24f — and Sean Cleary-Farrell (7) gets a weight allowance that aids a horse who travels prominently and has the stamina profile to see out 2m7f strongly; the tongue-strap is a familiar piece of equipment.|

runners_data.name: Survivors Sister
runners_data.note: Paul Gilligan's 7yo hasn't run for 108 days and her record shows just two placed efforts from eight starts on Good or similar; maps as prominent but her form string (1P7-39) is too inconsistent to inspire confidence on this return from a lengthy absence.|

races.paceDynamic: Affinity Rock is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no other genuine pace-setter to challenge her, she should stride into an uncontested lead and control tempo from the outset over this stamina-testing 2m7f on Good To Yielding ground at Ballinrobe. Giorgia Rose and Straight Home will press forward to occupy prominent positions just behind, creating a steady, sustainable gallop rather than a burning fractions scenario — this trip and ground combination rewards honest rhythm over sprint finishes. The field holds more hold-up types than the race shape can naturally accommodate; Ad Caelum and Carried With Love are genuine closers who are likely to be redistributed into midfield rather than their preferred rear positions, and both face a tougher task than their natural style would suggest, with Joya Del Mar and Cooke's Lass also competing for limited late-race real estate. This race shape — a single, uncontested leader setting an honest but measured gallop — most strongly favours prominent racers who can track the pace and pounce from a handy position, with Giorgia Rose and Straight Home ideally placed to do so.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Affinity Rock Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Affinity Rock gains an uncontested lead and dictates a measured gallop that suits her stamina profile over 2m7f on Good To Yielding.
scenarios.body: Affinity Rock settles into her own rhythm with no rival willing or able to pressurise her, and the prominent duo of Giorgia Rose and Straight Home track her through the race without forcing a pace injection. Prominent horses who travel comfortably and can sustain their effort over the extended trip benefit most, as there is no late-race sprint on ground that gradually saps reserves.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Strike Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is honest enough to stretch Affinity Rock and Straight Home and/or Giorgia Rose time their runs to overhaul her before the last.
scenarios.body: A genuine 2m7f gallop on Good To Yielding softens the field sufficiently for a well-judged prominent ride to pick off a tiring leader in the straight, rewarding horses who have tracked efficiently without burning petrol. Straight Home's strong course and distance winning record and Giorgia Rose's consistency at the trip make them the primary beneficiaries of this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is strong enough to open a gap for a horse finishing from off the pace to close down the leaders in the final stages.
scenarios.body: Joya Del Mar, with the best proven record at this trip and in this going band, is the most realistic hold-up candidate to deliver a late challenge given her two wins at 22f on Good or similar; Cooke's Lass, absent 364 days, is a bigger risk but holds claims on her best form. Note that Ad Caelum and Carried With Love, though strong closers by nature, are squeezed into midfield roles by the race shape and face a compromised effort, reducing the probability of this scenario materialising.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Turns Messy/Attrition
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors, falls or a slow early pace causes a scramble in the home straight with no horse having a clear advantage.
scenarios.body: A beginners' steeplechase over nearly 3 miles introduces meaningful jumping risks — Cherry Red has shown a tendency to fade and has had jumping issues, while long-absent Cooke's Lass (364 days off) could add chaos if she jumps poorly. Any such disruption opens the race to whichever horse jumps cleanest and stays out of trouble, favouring experienced course types.

watchPoints.text: Affinity Rock's ability to control tempo unchallenged is the pivotal factor — if she gets away cleanly at the first fence and settles, the race is likely run to her strengths; watch for any early crowding from Giorgia Rose or Straight Home pressing her sooner than expected.

Cooke's Lass (364 days off) is the biggest X-factor in the field — Gordon Elliott runners can return fit, but a near-year absence in a beginners' chase at 2m7f means her jumping fluency is untested and she could unsettle the race shape if she makes errors.

Ad Caelum and Carried With Love are true hold-up horses forced into midfield by the race shape — if neither can find a position further back than they're mapped, they will use more energy than ideal tracking the pace, potentially flattening their finishing efforts.

Cherry Red's finishing pattern — fading late — is a key flag in a stamina test of 2m7f on Good To Yielding ground; watch whether she jumps cleanly early but struggles to sustain her effort from three out, which could interfere with horses tracking her in midfield.

The apprentice/claimer factor is notable with three conditional/amateur riders (Alan O'Sullivan 5lb, Carl Millar 5lb, Sean Cleary-Farrell 7lb, Alix Balfe 7lb) — watch for any positional inexperience at the early fences that reshapes the order before the race settles into its natural rhythm.

races.name: Lodge At Ashford Castle Handicap Steeplechase

runners_data.name: Il Silenzio
runners_data.note: Strong staying form over 25f on soft/good, two wins at the trip, and the claiming jockey Conor Smithers (7) keeps the weight low at 168lbs; a natural hold-up horse who will be ridden patiently and needs a strong gallop or a clean wide passage — the steady pace here is a concern, but sim-going record of 11/12 is excellent.

runners_data.name: Ladies Well
runners_data.note: Six-year-old with a remarkable sim-going record of 14/14 and three wins from five on comparable surfaces; held up by Alan O'Sullivan and has won at 22-24f, so the step to 2m7f is a query, but she travels well and can be ridden prominently enough to offset the trip concern.

runners_data.name: Fr Gilligansvoyge
runners_data.note: Thirteen-year-old veteran in sparkling form — 1-3-2-1-2 in last five, all on good ground, and the 2m6f win last time out fits this 2m7f trip well; prominent racer for Sarah Kavanagh who can sit close to Kilashee and benefit directly from the uncontested pace scenario — natural style matches the dominant race shape.

runners_data.name: Mistyburn
runners_data.note: Hold-up six-year-old with a 1W/3P sim-going record over 22-25f on good, but recent form shows a drop in level after wins — 6-6-3 trend; Mr R Sugrue (7) claims weight and the horse stays well, but needs something to close into off a steady pace.

runners_data.name: Reve Inoui
runners_data.note: 97-day absence is a significant concern, and form figures of PP54-8 suggest this campaign has been difficult; promoted runner going OK on ground but the sim-going record of 0W/0P with no placing on comparable surface is damning for a wide-open race.

runners_data.name: Las Brisas Boy
runners_data.note: Five-year-old hold-up type with a fading-in-finish flag — placed twice at 20f on good but those efforts were at a shorter trip and the step to 2m7f is unproven; Kieren Buckley rides, and the finishing tendency to weaken late is a real worry in a steadily-run stamina test.

runners_data.name: Zolpharine
runners_data.note: Bolted up twice at 22f earlier in the season (1-1 run), and Harry Sexton (7) keeps weight off; sim-going 11/15 with 2W/3P is solid, and while the hold-up style is naturally disadvantaged by the slow pace, ability and recent winning form make this a serious player if it gets a gap.

runners_data.name: Hit The Frame
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse with a 15/15 sim-going record — the best in the race on that metric — but 118 days off the track is a major question mark; naturally backmarker in style but redistributed to midfield on the map because the field is saturated with closers, meaning its chance is contingent on a stronger pace than Kilashee alone is likely to generate.

runners_data.name: The Little Yank
runners_data.note: Eleven-year-old veteran returning just four days after a run, which demands scrutiny; his natural style is to race from off the pace but the overcrowded rear means he'll be pushed closer than ideal — the style-fit discount and recent form of P-3370 combine to limit expectations, though he handles the going.

runners_data.name: Tomas O Maille
runners_data.note: Poor recent form of 9P9P83 across shorter trips tells a concerning story, and this longer 2m7f trip is new territory; a genuine hold-up horse repositioned to midfield on the map — the redistribution reflects the overcrowded rear rather than any tactical upgrade, and his form profile doesn't argue for optimism.

runners_data.name: Not So Serious
runners_data.note: Five-year-old with a staying-on win at 22f but form otherwise littered with Ps and a fatigue flag; redistributed from the rear because so many hold-up types are competing for the same ground — the fades-in-finish warning compounds the concern in a 2m7f test.

runners_data.name: Kilashee
runners_data.note: The sole front-runner in the race, OR=80 and aged 11, with recent form of PP after two pulls-up; his value here is entirely as a pace-maker rather than a winner — he controls the race shape but his own finishing prospects look limited based on recent runs.

runners_data.name: Swing Time
runners_data.note: Modest form across the board — 858P-6 — and sim-going record of 0W/0P with no placing on comparable surface; naturally holds up but pushed forward on the map due to overcrowding at the rear, and there is no angle here that points toward a competitive performance.

runners_data.name: Set The Tone
runners_data.note: Consistent younger horse with a 1W/3P sim-going record and placed effort at 22f in recent starts; a natural hold-up type whose redistribution to midfield could inadvertently suit if the field fans out — form figures of 0P2162 show a competitive animal who handles the ground, and the trip looks within range.

runners_data.name: Three Tribes
runners_data.note: Form of 0P1-PP is alarming, with the fades-in-finish flag adding another layer of doubt over 2m7f; natural hold-up type pushed forward on the map, but the absence of any encouraging recent data makes this a difficult proposition even in a wide-open field.

runners_data.name: Subset
runners_data.note: Twelve-year-old returning from 470 days off the track — that absence alone makes it almost impossible to assess; hold-up style, fades-in-finish flag, and a career record showing struggles at long trips combine to make this a significant risk at OR=72.

runners_data.name: Walkmethroughit
runners_data.note: No jockey listed, sim-going record of 0W/0P on comparable surfaces, and form of 77PP-7 offers nothing to work with; hold-up type redistributed to midfield on the map — there is no positive angle to construct here.

runners_data.name: Island McCoo
runners_data.note: Unattached to a named jockey in the data but boasts a strong sim-going record of 13/15 with 2W/3P; form of 421845 shows consistent competitiveness, and the hold-up style over this trip on similar ground puts it in the frame if it gets a run — a quiet each-way type in this scenario.

runners_data.name: U Asking Me
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old with a perfect 15/15 sim-going record — second only to Hit The Frame in that metric — but recent form of -7P08F includes falls and pulled-ups; hold-up type redistributed forward due to field saturation, and while the going suitability is impeccable, current form trajectory does not inspire confidence.

races.paceDynamic: Kilashee is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 19-runner field and, crucially, faces no meaningful pace pressure — no other genuine lead horse is identified, meaning he can dictate entirely on his own terms at whatever tempo suits him over 2m7f on Good to Yielding ground. With Kilashee able to control fractions from flag to finish, the pace is likely to be steady-to-sustainable rather than searching, which compresses the field and makes it harder for true hold-up horses to generate momentum off the final bend. The overwhelming majority of this field — Il Silenzio, Ladies Well, Mistyburn, Zolpharine, Island McCoo and many others — are hold-up or midfield types, and with only one horse willing to lead, prominent racers who can travel close to the steady gallop without burning fuel early hold the clearest positional advantage. This race shape strongly favours horses who settle in the first third of the field and travel smoothly into contention, rather than those who need a strong pace to close into — note that the field contains far more hold-up types than the pace map can accommodate at the rear, with Tomas O Maille, The Little Yank, Hit The Frame, Set The Tone, Swing Time and others all redistributed to midfield because they cannot realistically secure their natural backmarker position in this traffic.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Kilashee Dictates, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Kilashee leads at a steady clip and the field strings out conservatively, allowing a prominent or close-tracking horse to stalk and strike.
scenarios.body: Kilashee sets an uncontested, comfortable tempo over the 2m7f trip, gifting horses who travel in the first four or five a decisive positional and energy advantage turning for home; on Good to Yielding ground with no searching pace, the winner is likely to emerge from those who were never far off the leader and simply outstayed a flagging front-runner.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Gets Lucky Break
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so sedate that the field bunches and a true hold-up horse gets a clean passage wide or on the outside to deliver a late run.
scenarios.body: A dawdle up front compresses the field and eliminates the positional disadvantage of back-markers, allowing a horse with high ability like Il Silenzio or Island McCoo to weave through or swing wide and finish strongly; the Good to Yielding ground rewards stamina and a horse arriving late with a full tank could pick up the weakening pack.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Kilashee Fades, Chaos Erupts
scenarios.trigger: If Kilashee's front-running effort over 2m7f proves unsustainable and a late collapse of the leader triggers a scrambling finish between several mid-pack types.
scenarios.body: Without a genuine gallop to aim at, a mid-race surge from prominent types as Kilashee weakens creates an uneven pace that suits horses with tactical flexibility over pure hold-up closers; Fr Gilligansvoyge's consistent form and Mistyburn's stamina profile make them the best-placed to absorb the disruption.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Type Breaks Through
scenarios.trigger: If the field fans wide on the final circuit and a redistributed hold-up horse secures an unexpectedly prominent early position, racing closer than its natural style.
scenarios.body: A horse such as Set The Tone or Tomas O Maille, forced closer to the pace than usual by the bunched nature of a slow-run race, could find itself in an unintentionally perfect stalking position and sustain the effort home over the stamina-testing 2m7f; the style-fit discount applies but the compressed pace map means the gap between natural and redistributed positioning narrows.

watchPoints.text: Kilashee's pace is the engine of the entire race — if he is pulled up or eased early (form: PP), the race loses its only genuine shape-setter and a chaotic false-gallop becomes likely, scrambling all scenario probabilities.

Fr Gilligansvoyge is 13 years old and ridden by a 7lb claimer Sarah Kavanagh — if the horse jumps poorly or the amateur jockey misjudges the early pace, a horse best-positioned by its prominent style could lose that advantage immediately.

With over a dozen hold-up types competing for the same ground from 2m7f on Good to Yielding, watch for significant crowding and interference on the final bend — horses wide of the pack (Il Silenzio, Zolpharine) could gain a clear passage advantage over those trapped on the rail.

Ladies Well's trip stamina is unproven beyond 24f — if she begins to tire after the second-last, the horses who have been held up deepest and arrive freshest (Il Silenzio, Island McCoo) could swoop past her close home.

The sim-going records of Il Silenzio (11/12), Ladies Well (14/14) and Fr Gilligansvoyge (15/15) are all elite — on a day when the entire card is Good to Yielding, these three are the clearest ground-proven performers and any market drift away from them should be treated with caution.

races.name: Adare Manor Opportunity Handicap Steeplechase

runners_data.name: Leave In Secret
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed front-runner who holds the key to the pace map; recent form figures of 7-7432 are modest but the horse has course-applicable good-ground stats (13 wins/places from 15 on similar going) and James Smith allows it to stride on — the STYLE_FIT flag hints it may be operating slightly out of its comfort zone at the head of a 19-runner field, which should temper confidence beyond its tactical role.

runners_data.name: Mo Ghille Mar
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced five-year-old who bolted up 14 days ago at 1m6f on good ground; Harry Sexton (4lb claimer) retains the ride, and the headgear flag (p) adds a conditioning note — hold-up style suits if the pace fires enough to set up a late run, and 14 days between runs is tight but trainer Hanlon has won 1 from 16 over the fortnight.

runners_data.name: Lady Doyanne
runners_data.note: De Bromhead's hold-up mare has placed in four of her last five on good ground (1W4P from 8 on similar going) and drops back from a win trip, but the consistent form figures of 2-2-3-4 in similar company suggest she always runs her race — Alan O'Sullivan's 2lb claim is a useful booking and the tendency to be held up becomes a mild concern if the pace is truly sedate.

runners_data.name: Farrokh
runners_data.note: Prominent type dropping back in trip after winning at 1m6f on good ground 14 days ago; Liam McKenna's booking gives no weight relief and trainer Barry Connell's T14 is 0/4, but the recent win confidence and good-ground specialism (15/15 on similar going, 1W8P) means he should travel prominently and test the pace dynamic around the home turn.

runners_data.name: Ballybrittas
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with a course-relevant win (1/16f/GOO) in recent form and solid consistency stats (12/12 on similar going, 2W5P); Mr R Sugrue (4lb) keeps the weight light but this horse has form at 2m and may find 2m1f on the sharp side of ideal given the hold-up style.

runners_data.name: Claude
runners_data.note: Five-year-old hold-up type fitted with tongue-tie and blinkers, running 29 days after a modest return (form 0-3-0-4); the going stats show 11 efforts on similar ground with only 1W3P, and trainer Sarah Connell has had no runners in the last 14 days — the form figures lack urgency and this is a horse to oppose if the pace map stays compact.

runners_data.name: Custers Mistake
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old returning after a 401-day absence, which is a significant fitness question despite winning at 1m20f on good ground previously; form of 1-2 in its last two completed starts (2W5P on similar going) is attractive on paper but the layoff is a dealbreaker unless trainers have given this horse a very prep-ready profile.

runners_data.name: Stoneyford Lady
runners_data.note: De Bromhead's prominent mare with tongue-tie and cheekpieces, racing 45 days after her last run; going form of 13/15 similar conditions (1W5P) is workmanlike and Danny Power's 4lb claim helps the weights — she is a genuine prominent type who will try to track Leave In Secret but form figures of 5-3-4 suggest she finds one or two too good.

runners_data.name: Sayitfirst
runners_data.note: Veteran hold-up type at OR 98 and ten years old, with solid going stats (15/15 similar, 1W4P) and two consecutive placed efforts — Michael Kenneally rides without a claim, and the age combined with form figures of 2-2-9-P-8 suggest consistency at this level but limited ceiling for improvement.

runners_data.name: Poppycon
runners_data.note: Prominent type with headgear (tp) racing 35 days after a blank return, and no wins from 8 on similar going (0W3P) is a concern; Paddy Cody's 4lb claim keeps the weight competitive but the absence of a win strike-rate at this level makes this a follow-the-race angle rather than a primary interest.

runners_data.name: Bossing It
runners_data.note: Josh Williamson partners a genuine hold-up horse that has been redistributed into midfield on the map — in truth this runner prefers to come from the back, and in a field of this size getting a clear passage may prove difficult; T14 of 0/1 and a STYLE_FIT flag of 0.91 both temper expectations, though a placed effort two back shows ability at this level.

runners_data.name: Fedneys Park
runners_data.note: De Bromhead's prominent type running 89 days after a poor sequence (0-0-4-0-0); the fade-in-finish flag is a serious concern in this distance range on Good to Yielding ground — the T14 of 4/26 suggests stable is in decent form but this horse's own figures don't encourage.

runners_data.name: Le Diablo
runners_data.note: Lightly-weighted five-year-old who ran only 11 days ago; a genuine hold-up type displaced into a midfield slot because the field is packed with closers — Kevin Healy (4lb) is a live booking and the recent form figures include a 2nd and 3rd, but the short turnaround and style displacement combine to cap confidence.

runners_data.name: Phoenix Arizona
runners_data.note: Thomas O'Connor (4lb) rides a horse whose natural style is to close from off the pace — with multiple redistributed closers in this field, it will struggle to settle where it wants; recent form of 2/18f and 3/18f show it stays well and finds the frame, but the 93 OR and crowded rear of field make it difficult to assess the winning chance clearly.

runners_data.name: Itsalonglongroad
runners_data.note: Twelve-year-old veteran prominent type running 26 days after a moderate return, fitted with a hood; going stats are fine (14/15 similar, 1W5P) but age and recent form (5-P-0-7-3) suggest this is a horse working to complete rather than win, and the trip at 2m1f is consistent with past targets.

runners_data.name: Roccabaker
runners_data.note: 145-day break is the immediate flag for David Harry Kelly's hold-up type, displaced on the map from its preferred rear position; two wins from 14 on soft-related ground but the last completed run was a pull-up, and returning from nearly five months off into a 19-runner field asks serious fitness questions.

runners_data.name: Political Stance
runners_data.note: The fade-in-finish flag reinforces what the form figures (0-7-2-P-0) already say — this is a horse who gets into contention and then empties; displaced from its natural hold-up position into midfield on the map, and T14 of 1/5 won't override the concern about finishing ability at this trip.

runners_data.name: Feet On The Ground
runners_data.note: Fitted with a hood and carrying the lowest competitive weight at 142lbs, this hold-up type has never won on good ground (0W5P from 14 runs on similar); displaced into midfield from its true back-of-field position, and trainer Hannon has had no runners in the past 14 days — the 66-day gap adds uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Coole Vision
runners_data.note: The combination of a fade-in-finish flag, 0W0P from 10 runs on similar going, no wins recorded in recent form (4-P-0-0), and displacement from a true hold-up position into midfield makes this the hardest horse in the field to frame a positive argument for — OR of 75 reflects the current level of ability.

races.paceDynamic: Leave In Secret is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 19-runner field and, crucially, looks set to enjoy an uncontested lead — Farrokh and Stoneyford Lady will press from prominent positions but neither is a true pace-forcing type, meaning Leave In Secret can control fractions on Good to Yielding ground without being seriously pressured. That sustainable, dictated gallop through 2m1f of Ballinrobe's flat, galloping circuit will produce a race run at an even clip rather than a breakneck pace — conditions that reward those who travel comfortably in the first half and have something in reserve at the second-last. The field holds far more true hold-up types than the map can place at the rear — Bossing It, Phoenix Arizona, Le Diablo, Roccabaker, Political Stance, Feet On The Ground and Coole Vision are all genuine closers pushed into midfield, meaning not all will secure their preferred position, and those best able to adapt will be advantaged. With a single untroubled pace-setter and a moderate gallop forecast, this race shape most favours prominent-to-midfield runners who can travel within striking range and produce a sustained finish from the home turn — a seat just off Leave In Secret or just behind the leaders is the golden ticket here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Leave In Secret bowls along uncontested and the race is run at a steady-to-moderate gallop throughout.
scenarios.body: Leave In Secret sets a controlled tempo that keeps the race together until the final circuit, and prominent/handy types who travel fluently are delivered into contention from the second-last without needing a turn of foot on testing ground.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Handy Types Grind Clear
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely modest and the race develops into a stamina test through the last half-mile.
scenarios.body: The lack of pressure through the early and middle stages means horses racing close to the pace in a handy position simply outstay rivals who have been held up and cannot quicken on Good to Yielding turf.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Finish Fast
scenarios.trigger: If Leave In Secret is pressured unexpectedly and the pace lifts, draining those who raced prominently.
scenarios.body: A stronger-than-expected gallop burns out the handy brigade late on, and genuine hold-up horses who actually managed to settle in their natural position late come through in the final 100 yards — though several redistributed runners will not be in true closing positions.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prominent Horse Outstays Field
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is very slow early and then quickens sharply from three out, creating a war of attrition from the home turn.
scenarios.body: A slow-fast gallop catches out hold-up horses who cannot bridge the gap and rewards the runner who is travelling best jumping the second-last with a clear view and enough petrol — going fitness and jumping accuracy become decisive.

watchPoints.text: Leave In Secret (uncontested lead) — watch whether Farrokh or Stoneyford Lady push up to challenge in the first mile; if they do and the pace lifts unexpectedly, the entire pace map shifts and prominent types will be punished.

Bossing It, Phoenix Arizona, Le Diablo and Roccabaker are all true hold-up horses mapped into midfield — in a 19-runner field on a flat galloping track, watch for traffic congestion from the home turn if the pace bunches, as these horses may be left with nowhere to go at the critical moment.

Custers Mistake returns after 401 days off — watch the betting market in the hour before the race; any significant support would suggest a well-prepared return, but uninformed punters should treat it as an unknown fitness variable.

Mo Ghille Mar runs only 14 days after a win and wears headgear — watch its behaviour in the paddock and early jumping for signs of freshness or over-keenness, which could compromise a hold-up plan in a large field.
